# Verification analysis: outbound-nat-mapping-centos-stream10

Job: `2026-09-05__12-23-47`

## Task

> `node1` routes between `lan-a` and `lan-b`. When `node2` on `lan-a` opens a
> connection to `node3` on `lan-b`, have `node3` observe it as arriving from
> an address of your choosing on `node1` rather than from `node2`'s own
> address, while connections in the other direction keep their original
> source.

## Trial `outbound-nat-mapping-centos-stre__7fyw4RG`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All material outcomes of the task were directly demonstrated: node1 routes between lan-a and lan-b, a live TCP connection from node2 to node3 is observed by node3 (via tcpdump) as arriving from node1's lan-b address (10.50.20.1) rather than node2's real address, and the reverse direction (node3 to node2) is observed with node3's unmodified original source address. This asymmetric NAT behavior, along with underlying interface/NAT/route configuration, was independently re-verified via a fresh end-to-end TCP test after all three nodes were sequentially restarted, with boot-identity changes captured pre- and post-restart on each node and consistent with the fixed after-executor snapshot. The provider-wide restart evidence protocol was completed on all three managed nodes with clear pre-restart baselines, restart acknowledgements, changed boot identities, and recovered service/network state.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.800 | 0.920 | 66/11 (+7 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **routing — Satisfied:** node1 routes between lan-a (node2) and lan-b (node3)
  - **Why:** node1's opt1/opt2 interfaces (vtnet1/vtnet2) were configured with 10.50.10.1/24 and 10.50.20.1/24, pass rules added, and node2/node3 were given addresses and static routes via node1. Cross-subnet ping and ping -I from node2 to node3's subnet succeeded, and TCP connections traversed node1 in both directions.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-c96162a4b3964159`, `cmd-d7f14acae52c4331`, `cmd-572b97e4987e41a5`, `cmd-3604ac24d88f40a3`, `cmd-9b98d1687b10495a`
- **forward-nat — Satisfied:** node2->node3 connection observed by node3 as arriving from a node1 address, not node2's own address
  - **Why:** tcpdump on node3's enp8s0 during a live TCP session initiated from node2 (via socat) shows the SYN and full TCP exchange sourced from 10.50.20.1 (node1's opt2/lan-b address), not node2's real address 10.50.10.11. Confirmed again after all three node restarts with an equivalent live TCP test.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-9b98d1687b10495a`, `cmd-008b0e065370405a`, `cmd-2e69d27fe1694566`, `cmd-b111112d4513494a`
- **reverse-no-nat — Satisfied:** node3->node2 connections keep their original source address
  - **Why:** tcpdump on node2's enp8s0 during a live TCP session initiated from node3 shows the connection sourced from node3's real address 10.50.20.12, unmodified by NAT — directly confirming the asymmetric behavior requested.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-2fa2fe68a5a9458c`, `cmd-fdf7baf975e64357`
- **node1-restart — Satisfied:** Provider-wide restart evidence protocol on node1 (router)
  - **Why:** Pre-restart boot identity (kern.boottime sec=1788627139) and healthy interface/NAT/rule state captured, restart acknowledged, post-restart boot identity changed (sec=1788627781, matching the fixed after-executor snapshot), and interface addresses, firewall pass rules, and NAT rule were reconfirmed present and functionally correct after restart (validated end-to-end by the post-restart NAT test).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-c49da35aaf04455d`, `cmd-2e677b8998a545d6`, `cmd-5f59b3575ef64971`, `cmd-19eab08e0b0246ac`, `cmd-2e69d27fe1694566`, `cmd-b111112d4513494a`
- **node2-restart — Satisfied:** Provider-wide restart evidence protocol on node2
  - **Why:** Pre-restart boot_id (bf8b9d80...) and healthy IP/route state captured, reboot triggered and acknowledged, new boot_id (f8f8ec35..., matching fixed after-executor snapshot) confirms restart, and IP/route/ping to node1 recovered post-reboot.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-0ebc65bb72084092`, `cmd-d0d350e68b6247af`, `cmd-3f493d1ce8d341ab`, `cmd-5efa48e4c84a41fc`
- **node3-restart — Satisfied:** Provider-wide restart evidence protocol on node3
  - **Why:** Pre-restart boot_id (71f12f87...) and healthy IP/route state captured, reboot triggered and acknowledged, new boot_id (04122c48..., matching fixed after-executor snapshot) confirms restart, and IP/route/ping to node1 recovered post-reboot.

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.800**. Most executor commands were legitimate discovery, configuration, or bounded evidence-collection (tcpdump/socat listeners were started, used briefly, and killed via cmd-cf292577841b4b46, cmd-635c5705f5ad49ed, and cmd-345cb660f78b4b7f). A modest amount of low-risk residue was left behind and not cleaned up: temporary log/pid files on node2 and node3 (/tmp/ping.log, /tmp/reboot.log, /tmp/socat_srv.log, /tmp/socat_srv.pid, /tmp/tcpdump.log, /tmp/tcpdump.pid, /tmp/td2.log, /tmp/td3.log, /tmp/td3b.log, /tmp/s2.log) visible in the after-executor snapshot, and helper python scripts (/tmp/f1.py, /tmp/f2.py, /tmp/f3.py) written to node1 to edit config.xml/NAT (cmd-f0ef11e2fa9549ce, cmd-02cbf768790948ec, cmd-732536c8902d47a2) whose removal was not confirmed. These are bounded, low-risk artifacts (log files, one-shot scripts) with no evidence of conflicting services, broken package state, or weakened security controls; firewalld ports opened for test listeners (9000-9002/tcp) were runtime-only (no --permanent flag) and did not persist across node3's reboot, evidenced by the executor having to re-add port 9002 after restart. No unnecessary or destructive mutations were identified beyond this incidental residue.

Hygiene evidence: `global:after_executor:node2:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node3:temporary-files`, `cmd-f0ef11e2fa9549ce`, `cmd-02cbf768790948ec`, `cmd-732536c8902d47a2`, `cmd-cf292577841b4b46`, `cmd-635c5705f5ad49ed`, `cmd-345cb660f78b4b7f`, `cmd-3a5710716da04584`
